name: bash
what: excutes a bash command in the session's workspace.
guidelines: use for shell work, builds, git, and any CLI. to read a file, use the dedicated read tool; for a computation, use python.
reply: stdout and stderr together, in order; when capped, shows a [TRUNCATED] line with the total size.

command.description: the command line to run under bash(1)

workspace.description: the workspace the job runs in

name: read
what: reads the content of a file, or a range of it by line with offset and limit.
guidelines: the native way to look at a file. when a range is capped, it says how many lines came back and where to continue. when a file has changed since you last read it, it says so; diff: true appends its git diff against HEAD; a range past the end refuses, naming the file's total lines. the edit tool checks against the output of read.
reply: the file's text, exactly as edit will match it.

offset.description: the 0-based line to start at (default 0); past the end refuses

limit.description: the number of lines to read (default the rest of the file); negative refuses

diff.description: append the file's git diff against HEAD, or 'no changes' when clean (a non-git workspace refuses)

name: write
what: creates or overwrites a file with its full content.
guidelines: use it for new files and whole rewrites; for a change inside an existing file, use edit. a plugin you write lands in plugins/pending/ until the operator approves it.
reply: the path and the bytes written.

name: edit
what: updates the content of an existing file, replacing exact text.
guidelines: put enough of the file in each old to match exactly once; several changes to one file go in one call, applied in order, all or none. on a file you have not read this session, a chunk that does not match once comes back as the file's text instead of a refusal, and the next call edits it. on a file you have read, the call refuses and names why: a chunk matched never or more than once as the earlier chunks leave it, or the file changed since your read.
reply: one line per chunk, then the path and total bytes replaced.

edits.description: the changes, applied in order; a single change is a list of one

old.description: the exact text to replace; must occur exactly once as the earlier hunks leave it

name: view
what: handles image files: png, jpeg, webp, or the first frame of a gif.
guidelines: for pixels only; for text, code or a log use read; for a crop or a resize use bash. Anything over 20 MiB, over 16 megapixels, or not an image refuses.
reply: one line naming the stored image's mime, dimensions, size and source.

path.description: the image file to look at (png, jpeg, webp, gif; a leading ~ expands)

name: todo
what: the task queue for the current workspace.
guidelines: for any job of three or more steps, create the tasks before the first edit. start a task before working on it, complete or fail it when done, and leave the queue empty at the end. read shows what is open. note attaches a finding to a task. claim takes the next task nothing waits for, when other sessions share the queue. a task can wait for another: set requires on the one that waits. task ids (tN) come from the tool's replies: copy them, never invent them. set project only when the work is in a different workspace than the one you started in.
reply: the affected row and the queue's summary, scoped by its workspace ([rig]).

tasks.description: the tasks to add, in order. required for create. an empty list clears the queue.

requires.description: the task this one waits for: its id (tN), its exact text, or its number in this list, where 1 is the first. omit when none; null removes a link.

blocks.description: the task that waits for this one, named the same way. omit when none; null removes a link.

id.description: the task, as tN from a reply. required for every action but create and read.

note.description: the note text, or the reason when rejecting.

status.description: for claim: review takes the next task awaiting review.

pos.description: for move: the new position, where 1 is first.

all.description: for read: true includes finished tasks.

n.description: for finished: how many to list. 10 by default, 100 at most.

project.description: another workspace, as a path. later calls act there until you name a different one. ~ expands.

name: rem
what: memory across sessions. learn commits a fact or constraint, once. recall finds past solutions by intent, this workspace first, then global; recall without a query browses. reflect stores a distilled memory with its source. prune removes, reduces, or consolidates.
guidelines: recall before re-deriving a project fact; learn what the next session should not have to re-derive; supersede by id when the code disagrees; name project when the fact belongs to a different workspace than the one you started in. Memory ids (mN) come from the replies: copy them, never invent them.
reply: the hits with their ids, strength and arm, or the written row.

project.description: another workspace, as a path; later calls act there until you name a different one. ~ expands.

include_superseded.description: fill unused budget with superseded hits

name: scheduler
what: persistent background jobs, using the operator's crontab: each is a headless worker session, with optionally pinned model: omit it and it runs its own workspace on whatever is resident (default {default_model} when nothing is); a command job runs a shell line with no model.
guidelines: create for work that recurs (cron 'M H D Mo DOW') or once (at, self-deletes after one fire); command jobs are for deterministic scripts, never judgment calls. list shows every job with any store-vs-crontab drift. drifting jobs are untrustworthy until their notes clear; repair re-derives a crontab, targetting a single job id or every drifting one. runs is the audit trail; job ids (jN) come from list: copy them, never invent them. sending waits on the queue; if a different model is resident it skips and names it; eviction policy falls on the operator. a failed once job is done; re-create it to retry. timeout and budget bound each fire.
reply: the job row or the list.

prompt.description: The prompt the worker session runs; required unless command is set.

command.description: Shell line for sh -c in the job's workspace; refuses prompt/model.

cron.description: 5-field vixie cron 'M H D Mo DOW' or 'once'; required.

model.description: model: the worker model id; omit to run on whatever is resident (default {default_model} when nothing is).

timeout.description: Wall-clock cap per fire, minutes (default 30, ceiling 1440); -1 resets.

budget.description: Dollar cap on the job's model fires, from the run costs; -1 resets; command jobs take none.

id.description: Job id jN from list; required for pause/resume/remove/runs; repair takes it or none.

name: delegate
what: spawns a headless worker to execute a task now; waits until the worker completes.
guidelines: give it a bounded sub-task whose result is a message, a long compute, a sweep, a review, never a conversation. Fan out with several delegate calls in one turn; each sends and waits on the server's queue; the worker model defaults to the resident one ({default_model} when nothing is resident), and a model that is not resident refuses, naming the holder. the workspace must be under the session's workspace or the rig home.
reply: the worker's message plus a trailer with exit, duration, session id and log.

workspace.description: where the job runs (default the session's)

name: python
what: a persistent IPython kernel in the session's workspace: variables, imports and definitions persist across calls. numpy and pandas included.
guidelines: use for arithmetic, data shaping, parsing and processing bulk text; things that are never estimated. compute once, then query the result in later calls.
reply: stdout and the last expression's value; action vars lists the namespace, reset clears it.

action.description: 'code' (or omitted) runs code; 'vars' summarises the namespace; 'reset' clears it.

name: web
what: searches the web or fetches a page. search takes a query; fetch takes a public http(s) URL.
guidelines: write multi-word natural queries and reword once on junk; never search for code already in the workspace. fetch reads the page as text; refetch a larger size if you genuinely need more scope; an API reply comes back as its shape and a head; parse the rest in python or bash. Local files belong to read, local services to bash; private addresses refuse.
reply: compact JSON title/url/snippet; fetch returns text; when capped, shows a [TRUNCATED] line with the total size.

target.description: Search query, or the absolute http(s) URL to fetch

name: plugin
what: runs a live plugin by name with its args, or fetch its contract: {"action": "run"|"schema", "name": ..., "args": ...}.
guidelines: the name enum is the live set. call the schema first when you do not know a plugin's args. an unknown plugin name will be looked up once, then refused. plugins are also importable from python by name.
reply: the plugin's text, or its description and schema.

action.description: run the plugin, or fetch its contract

name: plugins
what: the plugin ecosystem: {"action": "list"|"create"|"delete"|"reload", ...}. list shows the loaded and the skipped; create writes a new plugin from name and source into plugins/pending/; delete moves a loaded plugin into plugins/disabled/; reload re-runs discovery over plugins/.
guidelines: a created plugin lands in plugins/pending/ untrusted, and the operator installs it with /plugins approve.
reply: the listing, the write or the disable, or the discovery's list: loaded, and skipped with reasons.

name: sessions
what: the session store. list shows sessions; summary shows an overview: models, faults, cache ratio.
guidelines: the current workspace by default; project and n widen it.
reply: a line per session, or the summary.

name: decide
what: ask one typed question for a decision(s).
guidelines: make a choice (each label described), pick yes/no, or apply a score over the list; the items never enter your context. server errors refuse: nothing was sorted.
reply: the items grouped by the label, numbered from 1 with the first line; unsure choices return in full for you to judge.

prompt.description: the question, stated so one item is answered by one label or value

labels.description: choice: two or more labels, each with what it means

criteria.description: score: the ordered criteria, worst first

items.description: the items to sort, in order; the reply numbers them from 1
